title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

providers.name: Atlassian Jira / Confluence Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Product IP allowlisting requires Premium/Enterprise. SAML SSO typically requires Atlassian Guard Standard or an included entitlement.

controls.name: Service account API token expiration
controls.what: Admin picks a 1-365 day expiry when creating a service account API token (default one year).
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > Create credentials > API token
controls.quote: Select an expiration date for the API token. Token expiration can be between 1 and 365 days.

controls.name: Service account API token scopes
controls.what: Token scopes are chosen at creation and cannot be changed later.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > Create credentials > API token > scopes
controls.quote: Once you create an API token, you can’t modify its scopes. If you want to apply different scopes, you’ll need to create a new token.

controls.name: Revoke service account API token
controls.what: Revoked tokens stop working and are removed, within about 10 minutes.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > [account] > credentials > Revoke
controls.quote: When you revoke a token it no longer works and we permanently remove it from your account.

controls.name: Service account app roles and groups
controls.what: Admins choose which apps/roles and groups a service account has, which bounds what its credentials can reach.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > create/edit > roles, groups
controls.quote: Select roles for the app s that the service account needs to access. You can also add the service account to a group.

controls.name: Delete service account
controls.what: Deleting the account removes all its access and credentials.
controls.setting: Atlassian Administration > Directory > Service accounts > ••• > Delete account
controls.quote: When you delete a service account, this means the service account can no longer access any app s. We also delete the credentials associated with this service account.

controls.name: Create a service account (Organization admin only)
controls.what: Only organization admins can create service accounts and their credentials, so other users cannot mint these credentials.
controls.plan: Atlassian Guard Standard or Enterprise (5 service accounts free)

authentication.summary: A scoped API token issued to an organization service account. It is sent as a Bearer token (or Basic) to api.atlassian.com gateway URLs such as https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudId}/...; site URLs are not supported.

federation.details: This is a static token created in Atlassian Administration. Service accounts cannot be provisioned from an IdP and cannot sign in interactively.

ip_restriction.boundary: Product IP allowlists say they block programmatic API access, and API tokens are not in the exemption list. The docs do not name service-account tokens or the api.atlassian.com gateway explicitly, so test coverage. Allowlists need Premium (Jira, JSM, Confluence, Compass) or Enterprise (Analytics, Focus).

renewal.summary: The static token is reused on each request until it expires (1 to 365 days); an admin then creates a new token. No refresh token is involved.

administration.summary: Organization admins create and revoke tokens under Directory > Service accounts. Scopes are fixed at creation. Admins can see active tokens with creation, expiry and last-used dates. Deleting the service account removes its credentials.
administration.conditions: Five service accounts per organization are free; more need Atlassian Guard. Not available on Atlassian Government Cloud.

offboard.details: Service accounts are not tied to a person.

inventory.details: Directory > Service accounts > View API tokens shows active tokens, creation, expiry and last use, per service account.

network.ui: admin.atlassian.com > Security > Device security > IP allowlists > IP allowlist > select apps and IP ranges (test service-account token coverage)

reads.ui: Atlassian Administration > Insights > Audit log; filter activity "Viewed Jira issue" / "Viewed Confluence page" and actor = the service account

token_format.notes: Assumed same Atlassian API token family (ATAT prefix per Bamboo Javadoc); docs state variable length. Not separately confirmed for service accounts.

log_sources.name: Atlassian organization audit log (Admin > Insights > Audit log; Organizations REST API /v1/orgs/{orgId}/events and /events-stream)
log_sources.notes: Requires Atlassian Guard Standard/Premium or an Enterprise plan; 180-day retention, default view 7 days. API token activities only for managed (claimed-domain) accounts.

log_sources.name: Service accounts > View API tokens / API Access REST API GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/service-accounts/{serviceAccountId}/api-tokens
log_sources.notes: Per-service-account token inventory and recent usage.

credential_id_fields.notes: Atlassian account ID of acting user/service account

correlation_keys: ALQL: actor, "auth type", "ip address", site, app
anomaly_cues: ALQL "auth type" = api-token-service-account from a new IP/country
token creation on a service account by an admin who does not own the integration
token label/scopes mismatch the integration (e.g. write/delete scopes on a reporting bot)
use against site URLs (unsupported) suggests a different, possibly attacker, client
activity continuing more than 10 minutes after Revoked API token

containment.steps: Admin > Directory > Service accounts > select account > Credentials > Revoke; or DELETE /v1/orgs/{orgId}/service-accounts/{serviceAccountId}/api-tokens to revoke all; delete the service account.
containment.notes: Revocation can take up to 10 minutes to take effect. Permanent; reissue a new token.

sample_query.query: created >= "2026-09-12" AND "auth type" = "api-token-service-account" AND "ip address" !~ "203.0.113.*" ORDER BY created desc
sample_query.purpose: Find service-account API token use from outside the known egress range.
